e-8926.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 2x2 Matrix
e-8926.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/fd1cf7c3d929fb79576a59d4ef3aebd3f24a0d570c938ab80ebd44c5bd4c238f.png)

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
e-8926.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/b521c0b31d05de273d0abd37e00b046c0e36ed47ef30d22784a24cace4d676f9.png)

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 15 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 66\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=5 \\ 15{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=66.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $y_1=5$ and $y_2=-9.$ 

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/ccb4ab47d3a270cf9545d4f79e6f90b944cf6121fca3752eeee6ddc712fcfdec.png)

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
e-4777.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/7704f9285f14f496bb9f1721d188866c9464c585e33235c5cc6eee42e3f3a3eb.png)

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/712643d674cf8a7a086a9a935659d86bba7bd2fb25f131ec56e798cfc1d538d9.png)

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=2 \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=4 \\ {y}_{1}-2{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =2, \\ {y}_{2} & =4-{y}_{1} \\  & =4-(2) \\  & =2, \\ {y}_{3} & =1-{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\  & =1-(2)+2(2) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

e-4775.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization
e-4775.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/45cefb7311cd5253b76164cc7f2f3ce01b445f0e9061b720865227128b60debe.png)
If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 \cdot y_2?$
e-4775.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/b521c0b31d05de273d0abd37e00b046c0e36ed47ef30d22784a24cace4d676f9.png)

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/9dcc9f71745cce72ce7e122b3bc8cd7064d05f3be90d712202f42956956ef18e.png)
This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=6 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $y_1=6$ and $y_2=4.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/903fbfe6828526dace264d65baebf58c31e36db8a54e25ed1f3be859e6079ebb.png)

- Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/dcb234ae13cab2676ea5afa7fde452c870ff5088ff5748342c517bf2a96327a8.png)
This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $x_2=-2$ and $x_1=2.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14063081/assets/53bace542ba4dfd0d7e5e4bf9b6451c7f39502dd1bf24d030f654050629f0e0d.png)

Finally, $x_1 \cdot y_2 = 2 \cdot 4 = 8.$

after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=2 \\ -4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=2$ and ${y}_{2}=6.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$

Question 1
?

Consider the matrix L and the vector b, given by L=[10−41],b=[2−2]. If A=LU is the LU factorization of some 2×2 matrix A, find the vector y such that

{Ly=bUx=y is equivalent to Ax=b.

a
y=[22]
b
y=[26]
c
y=[24]
d
y=[2−2]
e
y=[02]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that since A=LU, we can write

Ax=b⟹(LU)⏟Ax=b.

Now, setting Ux=y, we obtain

L(Ux)⏟y=b⟹{Ly=bUx=y.

We now solve Ly=b. Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

[10−41][y1y2]=[2−2]. This gives the system of equations

{y1=2−4y1+y2=−2.

The solution to this system is y1=2 and y2=6.

Therefore, y=[26].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=2 \\ -4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=2$ and ${y}_{2}=6.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$

after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=0 \\ -6{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=0$ and ${y}_{2}=4.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=2 \\ 3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=2$ and ${y}_{2}=-9.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -9\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -10 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -36\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -10 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -36\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=7 \\ -10{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-36.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=7$ and ${y}_{2}=34.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 34\end{aligned}].$

Question 5
?

Consider the matrix L and the vector b, given by

L=[10−71],b=[5−2].

If A=LU is the LU factorization of some 2×2 matrix A, find the vector y such that

{Ly=bUx=y is equivalent to Ax=b.

a
y=[5−7]
b
y=[53]
c
y=[1−7]
d
y=[533]
e
y=[15]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that since A=LU, we can write

Ax=b⟹(LU)⏟Ax=b.

Now, setting Ux=y, we obtain

L(Ux)⏟y=b⟹{Ly=bUx=y.

We now solve Ly=b. Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

[10−71][y1y2]=[5−2]. This gives the system of equations {y1=5−7y1+y2=−2. The solution to this system is y1=5 and y2=33.

Therefore, y=[533].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 2x2 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=5 \\ -7{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=5$ and ${y}_{2}=33.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 33\end{aligned}].$

decision.explanation: Forward substitution gives y₁=−2, y₂=−1−(−2)=1, and −y₁−4y₂+y₃=−3. Thus 2−4+y₃=−3, so y₃=−1. Option b satisfies Ly=b.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-2 \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-1 \\ -{y}_{1}-4{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-2, \\ {y}_{2} & =-1-{y}_{1} \\  & =-1-(-2) \\  & =1, \\ {y}_{3} & =-3+4{y}_{2}+{y}_{1} \\  & =-3+4(1)+(-2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

$y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-7 \\ -{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=3 \\ 3{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-7, \\ {y}_{2} & =3+{y}_{1} \\  & =3+(-7) \\  & =-4, \\ {y}_{3} & =3-3{y}_{2} \\  & =3-3(-4) \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 15\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-7 \\ -{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=3 \\ 3{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-7, \\ {y}_{2} & =3+{y}_{1} \\  & =3+(-7) \\  & =-4, \\ {y}_{3} & =3-3{y}_{2} \\  & =3-3(-4) \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -4 \\ 15\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=9 \\ 7{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=7 \\ -9{y}_{1}+{y}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =9, \\ {y}_{2} & =7-7{y}_{1} \\  & =7-7(9) \\  & =-56, \\ {y}_{3} & =-1+9{y}_{1} \\  & =-1+9(9) \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -56 \\ 80\end{aligned}].$

Question 8
?

Consider the matrix L and the vector b, given by

L=[100710−901],b=[97−1].

If A=LU is the LU factorization of some 3×3 matrix A, find the vector y such that

{Ly=bUx=y

is equivalent to Ax=b.

a
y=[9−6381]
b
y=[−97080]
c
y=[9−5680]
d
y=[9−7080]
e
y=[−956−80]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that since A=LU, we can write

Ax=b⟹(LU)⏟Ax=b.

Now, setting Ux=y, we obtain

L(Ux)⏟y=b⟹{Ly=bUx=y.

We now solve Ly=b. Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

[100710−901][y1y2y3]=[97−1].

This gives the system of equations {y1=97y1+y2=7−9y1+y3=−1.

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

y1=9,y2=7−7y1=7−7(9)=−56,y3=−1+9y1=−1+9(9)=80.

Therefore, y=[9−5680].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=9 \\ 7{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=7 \\ -9{y}_{1}+{y}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =9, \\ {y}_{2} & =7-7{y}_{1} \\  & =7-7(9) \\  & =-56, \\ {y}_{3} & =-1+9{y}_{1} \\  & =-1+9(9) \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -56 \\ 80\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=3 \\ -4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-1 \\ 3{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =3, \\ {y}_{2} & =-1+4{y}_{1} \\  & =-1+4(3) \\  & =11, \\ {y}_{3} & =4-3{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2} \\  & =4-3(3)-2(11) \\  & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 11 \\ -27\end{aligned}].$

[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=3 \\ -4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-1 \\ 3{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =3, \\ {y}_{2} & =-1+4{y}_{1} \\  & =-1+4(3) \\  & =11, \\ {y}_{3} & =4-3{y}_{1}-2{y}_{2} \\  & =4-3(3)-2(11) \\  & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 11 \\ -27\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 9 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 9 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-2 \\ 9{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2 \\ -4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-2, \\ {y}_{2} & =-2-9{y}_{1} \\  & =-2-9(-2) \\  & =16, \\ {y}_{3} & =1+4{y}_{1}-{y}_{2} \\  & =1+4(-2)-(16) \\  & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 16 \\ -23\end{aligned}].$

Question 10

Consider the matrix L and the vector b, given by

L=[100910−411],b=[−2−21].

If A=LU is the LU factorization of some 3×3 matrix A, find the vector y such that

{Ly=bUx=y

is equivalent to Ax=b.

a
y=[24−11]
b
y=[2−8−3]
c
y=[−24−3]
d
y=[−216−23]
e
y=[−2−8−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that since A=LU, we can write

Ax=b⟹(LU)⏟Ax=b.

Now, setting Ux=y, we obtain

L(Ux)⏟y=b⟹{Ly=bUx=y.

We now solve Ly=b. Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

[100910−411][y1y2y3]=[−2−21].

This gives the system of equations {y1=−29y1+y2=−2−4y1+y2+y3=1.

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

y1=−2,y2=−2−9y1=−2−9(−2)=16,y3=1+4y1−y2=1+4(−2)−(16)=−23.

Therefore, y=[−216−23].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 9 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 9 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-2 \\ 9{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2 \\ -4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-2, \\ {y}_{2} & =-2-9{y}_{1} \\  & =-2-9(-2) \\  & =16, \\ {y}_{3} & =1+4{y}_{1}-{y}_{2} \\  & =1+4(-2)-(16) \\  & =-23.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 16 \\ -23\end{aligned}].$

after.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions of the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of the product ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=1 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=1$ and ${y}_{2}=4.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=4$ and ${x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{2}.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}=-\frac{3}{2}\cdot 4=-6.$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization
content.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions of the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of the product ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=1 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=1$ and ${y}_{2}=4.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=4$ and ${x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{2}.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}=-\frac{3}{2}\cdot 4=-6.$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization
content.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}7 & 3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions to the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=5 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=5$ and ${y}_{2}=14.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}7{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=5 \\ -2{x}_{2}=14.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=-7$ and ${x}_{1}=\frac{26}{7}.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}\frac{26}{7} \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{2}=\frac{26}{7}\cdot 14=52.$
